name: audio
description: A recording with its words: played with text-labelled controls (Play, Back 15 seconds, Forward 30 seconds, speed, a seek bar that says where it is in words), its length and size, a Download link, and its transcript under it, each line leading to the moment it was said and marked while it is heard.

use.when: a voice note, a meeting, a podcast or music is part of what the page holds: a file's own page, a note's recording.
use.not: a sound the page makes, such as an alarm, which is the clock's; or a video.
use.with: a transcript, which is what anyone who cannot hear it gets, and what search and the assistant read.

type.description: Its type, such as audio/mpeg, so a browser that cannot play it says so at once.

title.description: What it is, which names the player.

about.description: Its format and size in words: MP3 · 11 MB.

start.description: Seconds from the start, such as 12.50.

said.description: The same time in words, for a screen reader: 12 seconds.

text.description: What was said, and sounds such as [laughter].

cues.description: The transcript, a line per stretch of what was said, from its WebVTT.

none.description: What to say when there is no transcript yet, such as how one gets made.

make.description: Write it down now: where the recording's sound is sent to be written down on this computer. With auto, the page's script does it as soon as the page opens.

get.description: For the workspace's owner, when this computer has no speech-to-text: the press that gets it, saying how much it downloads.

size.description: How much it downloads, in words: 185 MB.

a11y.role: figure named by its title, holding the player (the browser's own, or buttons, a slider and a select) and the transcript as a list of links

keyboard.does: reaches Play, Back 15 seconds, Forward 30 seconds, the seek bar, Speed, Download, then each line's time in the transcript
on a button, plays or pauses, or skips; on a line's time, plays from there
on the seek bar, move 5 seconds (Up and Down arrows too)
on the seek bar, move a minute
on the seek bar, go to the start or the end
on Write it down, sends the recording to be written down on this computer; on Get speech-to-text, downloads it once

wcag.notes: Never plays by itself (1.4.2). The transcript is on the same page, under the player, with who spoke and the sounds that matter (1.2.1). Without a script the browser's own player is there and each line's time is a link into the recording (#t=). With it, the controls are buttons with their words in sight, not only icons (2.5.3), each at least 44 pixels (2.5.5); the seek bar says where it is in words, not a percentage, and while it has focus it moves only when moved, so it is not read out on every tick; starting one recording pauses any other on the page, so two never play over each other or a screen reader; a recording this browser cannot play says so in words, once, beside the Download link, in place of controls that do nothing; the line being heard is marked by a border and bold type as well as colour (1.4.1), is never announced, and the page is never scrolled to it. Nothing moves: no waveform. Writing a recording down happens on the computer that hosts the workspace; the press that gets speech-to-text says how much it downloads, from where, and that recordings never leave, and nothing is downloaded without it.

machine.identify: The audio element's src is the recording; each li[data-start] is one line of the transcript, its link's href ending #t=<seconds>.
machine.operate: Play by pressing Play, or set the audio element's currentTime from a line's data-start. A .sw-audio__trouble with words in it means this browser cannot play the recording; fetch its src instead. The transcript's words are also the file record's text.
